newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish NBP ups reserve on zloty term, forex depos.
newsitem.headline: Polish NBP ups reserve on zloty term, forex depos.

text.p: The National Bank of Poland said on Friday that from April 30 it would increase the obligatory reserve requirement on all foreign currency deposits to five percent from the current four percent.
The central bank also said in a statement it would increase mandatory reserves on zloty term deposits to 11 percent from the current nine percent on the same date.
"The NBP is raising the levels of obligatory reserves ...to further limit banks' credit expansion and to reduce internal demand and improve the trade balance situation," the bank said.
It said the mandatory reserve for zloty call deposits would remain unchanged. The rate is now at 20 percent.
The bank said the increase in zloty and currency required reserves should not reduce real interest rates on bank deposits.
